covers: Projected cost of the first two GPS III satellites ('up to $1.6 billion'), from US Government Accountability Office testimony of March 2012. Two satellites only: not the programme, not a per-satellite price.
source_name: Inside GNSS, 'Parts Testing Drives Up GPS III Program Costs, Forces Prime to Forego $70 Million Incentive Fee', 21 Apr 2012, citing GAO testimony GAO-12-563T

covers: Value of the production contract change for the seventh and eighth GPS III satellites, announced by the Pentagon on 31 Mar 2014. Two satellites, contract value to the maker; launch not included.
source_name: SpaceNews, 'U.S. Air Force Orders Two More GPS 3 Satellites', 1 Apr 2014

covers: Programme cost of the new ground control system for GPS III, up from 5.4 billion, from the Defense Department's Selected Acquisition Report for December 2017. Ground segment only: no satellites.
source_name: Air & Space Forces Magazine, 'New Report Highlights Soaring GPS III Costs', 4 Apr 2018

covers: Stated cost of carrying out the federal target programme for GLONASS from 2001 to 2011. Whole programme (satellites, ground, other); not split.
source_name: Russia Beyond (Rossiyskaya Gazeta), 'GLONASS benefits worth the extra expense', 16 Feb 2012

covers: Budget approved in 2012 for the federal target programme 2012 to 2020: planned, not money spent. Whole programme; not split.
source_name: Inside GNSS, 'GLONASS Plans 30 Satellites, Complete Augmentation System and Improved OCX by 2020', 30 Mar 2012 (same figure in the Russia Beyond article above)

covers: EU budget spent on the Galileo development phase before 2014, as listed by the European Court of Auditors. EU budget only: not the European Space Agency's or national spending.
source_name: European Court of Auditors, Special Report 07/2021 'EU space programmes Galileo and Copernicus', Annex I

covers: EU budget spent on the Galileo deployment phase up to the end of 2020 (2,473 before 2014 and 2,825 in 2014 to 2020). EU budget only; the Court does not say in the table what deployment contains.
source_name: European Court of Auditors, Special Report 07/2021, Annex I

covers: EU budget spent on Galileo and EGNOS (a regional augmentation service) together, up to the end of 2020; includes research and the EU agency. Not Galileo alone.
source_name: European Court of Auditors, Special Report 07/2021, Annex I

covers: No public total or per-satellite figure found in an official document or reputable press on 17 Oct 2026 (searched in English and Chinese). Industry output figures exist but are not what the system cost.
Financial sanction of May 2006 for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (NavIC): seven satellites and the ground infrastructure. A plan, not a final cost.
source_name: Comptroller and Auditor General of India, Report No. 2 of 2018, Department of Space chapter (seen through a press report, gisresources.com, 19 Mar 2018; the report itself could not be opened)

covers: About 1,284 crore of the 1,420 crore sanction spent by the time the audit report was tabled in Parliament on 13 Mar 2018. Spending on the programme only.

Planning estimate given on 17 Oct 2011 for a seven-satellite system, including launch and ground systems, by the secretary general of Japan's Strategic Headquarters for Space Policy. An estimate made before building; not a final cost.
source_name: SpaceNews, 'Japan Commits To Deploying Satellite Navigation System by 2020', 17 Oct 2011

covers: Planning estimate given at the same time for a four-satellite system, including launch and ground systems. An estimate made before building; not a final cost.
